title: Bring two stakeholders to the same conversation
why_matters: Half the work of a BA is reducing the number of game-of-telephone hops between the people who have the answer and the people who need it. Putting two stakeholders in the same room — for fifteen minutes, on a specific topic — is the single most efficient thing you can do this week. Even when it's awkward. Especially when it's awkward.
steps: Identify two people whose decisions are currently going through you because they don't talk to each other. Common pairs: PO + lead engineer, business sponsor + compliance, designer + customer success.
Pick one specific question both have a stake in. Avoid generalities ("alignment"); pick something concrete and decidable.
Book fifteen minutes with both. Write the question on the invite description. Don't soften it — the awkwardness is the point.
Facilitate. Stay quiet for at least the first three minutes. Take notes; send the summary same-day.
success_criteria: Two stakeholders have been in the same conversation for at least fifteen minutes. A decision (or a documented next step toward one) exists in writing. Both have received the summary.
reflection_prompt: What's the conversation you most want them to have next, and what would have to be true for it to happen without you in the room?
